summary: Four harnesses are structurally sound scaffolding but carry systemic weaknesses: byte-equivalence tests silently pass when binaries are absent (None-guard pattern), so CI can green without any real serialization; wasm-browser tests use JSON.stringify/crypto.createHash instead of WASM CBOR, meaning they never exercise WASM; Rust tests verify only round-trip, not canonical-byte output; endianness is not tested. Minor issues: no pytest fixtures/parametrize, mcp-compat lacks asyncio mode config, wasm-browser action duplicates setup-node, full-mode Makefile missing build target.

findings.issue: build target chains real toolchain calls (cargo, wasm-pack, npm) with no stub-mode guard; CI will fail on missing toolchain rather than skipping gracefully
test depends on build, so stub-only pytest run requires full Rust/Node toolchain even in CI stub mode
no build target defined; test target has no prerequisites, inconsistent with other harnesses
all: test alias is consistent across all four; .PHONY declarations are correct; verify: test chain is idempotent

test_rust_serializer_basic and test_byte_equivalence_rust_ts guard with 'if result:' — when binaries are absent both return None and the assertions are skipped entirely; tests pass vacuously in CI stub mode, defeating the harness purpose
no pytest fixtures or parametrize; test vectors are hardcoded rather than loaded from fixtures/stub.json via a fixture; adding a new vector requires code changes
serialize_with_wasm always returns None (import succeeds path is dead code — spec_from_file_location result is never used); WASM leg is untested

pytest-asyncio mode not configured; tests rely on implicit asyncio mode which requires pytest-asyncio >= 0.21 asyncio_mode='auto' or per-test mark; missing conftest.py with asyncio_mode setting may cause collection errors

test_golden_trace_format validates structure of static stub.jsonl but never compares live client output against the golden; the mutation-detection test only compares in-memory dicts, not persisted bytes

test_fixture_mutation_detection asserts original_sig == mutated_sig (slot changed, not signature); the test comment claims mutation detection but the assertion proves mutation is NOT detected in the signature field — logic is inverted
test_attestation_data_integrity uses JSON round-trip, not CBOR; does not match the CBOR serialization contract described elsewhere in the spec
MNEMONIC_MODE env var is set inside test function body without cleanup/teardown; can leak across test cases in the same process

test 'WASM serializer produces valid output' calls require('crypto') inside page.evaluate — Node.js built-ins are not available in a browser page context; this will throw and output will be null, but expect(output).toBeTruthy() may still pass if Playwright catches and returns null
no test ever imports or exercises the actual WASM module; tests only exercise JSON.stringify and in-memory object comparison — WASM byte-equivalence is not verified

playwright.config.ts sets workers: 1 in CI but fullyParallel: true globally; on CI these conflict — fullyParallel with workers:1 serializes all tests but the intent of fullyParallel is cross-file parallelism, making the CI config misleading
reporter: 'html' only; no list or line reporter for CI log output; failures are only visible by downloading the artifact
performance test threshold is 1ms per JSON.stringify call — this is not a WASM performance test
Cargo.toml is minimal and appropriate; edition 2021, clean dependency list (serde, ciborium, serde_json, hex)

lib.rs test only verifies round-trip structural equality (assert_eq!(original, decoded)), not that the encoded bytes match a canonical fixture hex string; a ciborium version bump that changes map ordering would pass the round-trip but break cross-language equivalence
serializer binary uses .expect() with panic on failure; exit code will be non-zero via panic output but stderr message is not propagated clearly to the Python test harness
no #[deny(warnings)] or clippy CI step configured in Cargo.toml or action
README documents the contract clearly: canonical-vectors.json injection path, hex comparison, stub format; contract is actionable
README documents JSONL format and RECORD=1 recording workflow; contract is clear
README describes wasm/pkg/ injection but does not specify the expected output format (hex string? Uint8Array?) that the browser test should compare against Rust output; contract is underspecified
README references 'fixtures/stub-attestation.json' in the stub fixture format section but this file does not exist; only stub-solana-tx.json and stub-arweave-tx.json are present
MNEMONIC_MODE=full activation path is documented; env var contract is clear

The Python harness compares hex strings output by Rust binary vs Node.js binary; this is string comparison of hex-encoded bytes, which is correct IF both outputs are canonically encoded. However the TS serializer uses the 'cbor' npm package while Rust uses ciborium — map key ordering between these libraries is not verified to be identical; a test with a multi-key struct would be needed

Endianness: CBOR integer encoding is big-endian by spec and both ciborium and cbor-js follow this; no explicit endianness test is present, and the stub fixture only uses u8 (version:1) and u64 (nonce:42) which fit in a single CBOR byte each, making endianness invisible in the current test vectors
The WASM leg (serialize_with_wasm) always returns None — three-way byte equivalence (Rust vs TS vs WASM) is never actually tested

stub.json fixture uses only two fields with small integer values; no multi-byte integer, string with unicode, nested map, or array is tested — these are the cases where serializer divergence typically occurs
All four actions use actions/checkout@v4 with fetch-depth: 0 and actions/upload-artifact@v4 with if: always() and retention-days: 30 — consistent structure

byte-equivalence and wasm-browser actions do not install Python or pytest, but byte-equivalence's make verify calls python3 -m pytest; the action will fail if Python is not pre-installed on the runner

wasm-browser action has two setup-node@v4 steps (lines 12-14 for base setup, lines 17-22 for cache); the first step is redundant and will cause a double-install warning; the cache step should replace, not duplicate, the base step
mcp-compat and full-mode actions pin Python to 3.11; byte-equivalence action omits a Python setup step entirely despite needing pytest

full-mode action passes inputs via env block but the python scripts read os.getenv directly with localhost defaults; the env: block in the action only applies to that specific run step, which is correct — but the independent verifier step has no env: block and will use localhost defaults regardless of action inputs
no outputs defined in any action; callers cannot inspect pass/fail status programmatically without parsing step exit codes

critical_issues: byte-equivalence Python tests pass vacuously when Rust/Node binaries are absent (None-guard pattern)
serialize_with_wasm always returns None — WASM leg is dead code
wasm-browser spec tests never load or call WASM; they test JSON.stringify only
Three-way byte equivalence (Rust vs TS vs WASM) is never exercised end-to-end
major_issues: Rust unit test asserts structural equality, not canonical byte output; cannot catch serializer drift across versions
Endianness invisible in stub fixture — all values fit in single CBOR bytes
full-mode README references stub-attestation.json which does not exist
byte-equivalence and wasm-browser composite actions omit Python/pytest setup steps
full-mode test_fixture_mutation_detection assertion logic is inverted
